PullRequest.Title: eslint: fix bracket notation in workbench services
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- replace identifier-safe bracket notation across the 23 allowlisted Workbench UI and remaining service files
- remove the cleaned group from `.eslint-allowed-bracket-notation-files`
- replace private-member bracket access in default-account tests with a typed test subclass and protected production seams

Stacked on #334756.

## Validation

- targeted ESLint: 24 changed source files
- targeted hygiene: 24 changed source files
- exact-scope audit: 23 removed allowlist entries plus one typed test-support file
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run transpile-client`
- `node --check src\vs\workbench\contrib\webview\browser\pre\service-worker.js`
- policy export integration: 2 passing
- encoding integration: 3 passing
- default account unit tests: 49 passing
- editor utilities/options unit tests: 15 passing
- update info parser unit tests: 21 passing
- workspace tags unit tests: 3 passing
- extension recommendations unit tests: 143 passing

## Known baseline drift

The Color Registry release test reports 1 passing and 2 failing checks because the generated known-variable list and `theme-color.md` are out of sync with currently registered colors and sizes. This PR does not include those unrelated generated/documentation updates.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench/editor configuration validation and extension menu/theme metadata rendering
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Editor option validation is synchronous before editor UI setup; command-table and theme-item property checks run when rendering extension details or theme choices. The changed accesses perform the same reads/writes as before and add nothing to the critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The fixed editor-option schema, plus the number of contributed commands/menu entries and themes already being rendered.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous in-memory object access and existing loops; the diff adds no tasks, promises, queues, or parallelism.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Static defaults and already-loaded manifest/theme objects are used directly. No cache key, invalidation, cold-load, or warm-load behavior changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: every changed expression is a static-key bracket access replaced by the equivalent dot access; surrounding loops and constructors are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; no additional CPU, allocation, I/O, or retained state is introduced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Work remains O(number of existing settings/commands/themes) with identical per-entry operations.

Scenarios.Scenario: Bulk-edit, call-hierarchy, and type-hierarchy pane state transitions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The data-state mutation occurs synchronously while showing loading, message, or populated UI. Existing tree/model loading remains on the same path and in the same order.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Mutate the existing element's data-state attribute, potentially triggering the same style invalidation as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One mutation per existing state transition, unchanged from before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same data-state attribute was assigned with bracket notation at the same points.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs on the UI path, but the bracket and dot forms invoke the same DOMStringMap setter and do not add layout, rendering, or repeated mutation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One DOM data-state write per pane state transition; hierarchy size controls unchanged tree work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new concurrency. Existing asynchronous tree setInput/expand work remains serialized as before, while each state mutation remains synchronous.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing hierarchy view-state maps and model references are unchanged; the property syntax does not alter reuse or disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the modified DOM assignments target the same receiver and literal property, and no surrounding control flow changed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser style cost varies by pane contents, but the diff does not change its frequency or mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; synchronous UI work is unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workspace tag discovery and workspace extension recommendation loading
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Cold workspace-tag resolution reads workspace metadata before returning tags; recommendation queries await the workspace config and then folder configs. The changed JSON/object member accesses occur after the same reads and parsing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check/read aiGeneratedWorkspaces.json, resolve workspace roots, and conditionally read recognized manifests such as package.json.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold tag resolution does one metadata exists/read pair, one grouped resolveAll over folders, and conditional per-folder manifest checks/reads; warm getTags calls use the existing _tags cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical filesystem calls and cache behavior; only literal-key bracket accesses were used.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold tag resolution awaits these operations; the changed aiGenerated/dependencies property access happens after their results and does not add calls.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve node_modules/pom.xml data for Azure workspace telemetry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One grouped node_modules resolve and up to one pom.xml exists/read pair per workspace folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same grouped/per-folder operations ran before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Telemetry work remains asynchronous and is not made more frequent by the tag property assignment changes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse the workspace configuration and each folder's .vscode/extensions.json.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one workspace configuration read, followed by one parallel read per workspace folder per existing API invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same files were read and parsed with bracket access to the same extensions key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Recommendation results await these reads, but the changed .extensions access does not alter their count or scheduling.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Workspace-tag file checks and reads scale with workspace folders and recognized manifest files; recommendation loading performs one workspace-file read plus one read per folder.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Workspace tags use existing resolveAll and Promise collections; folder recommendation files are read with Promise.all after the workspace config read. The diff does not alter grouping, serialization, or fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: WorkspaceTagsService caches the resolved tags in _tags after the first successful getTags call, so warm calls reuse them. Workspace extension configs are reread by existing APIs on demand. Neither lifecycle changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: direct call paths, cache ownership, and Promise grouping are visible; modified lines only select the same object fields.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Folder and manifest counts vary, but all scaling existed before the PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable boundary fan-out, cache, or concurrency regression.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The export command waits for configuration, obtains distro product data, merges policies, writes one output file, and exits. Changed property/env accesses do not move or add any operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read DISTRO_PRODUCT_JSON, or read package.json when selecting the distro revision.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One local product read, or one package.json read per command invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same branch and same single read used bracket property access.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before policy merge; unchanged by dot access to environment variables and extensionConfigurationPolicy.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch distro product.json from the GitHub API when no local product path is configured.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one request per export invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same request occurred after reading GITHUB_TOKEN with bracket notation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited on the export critical path, but neither its condition nor request count changes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write the serialized exported policy data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before process exit; unchanged by the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request native host process exit after completion or failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs after export completion and is unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of configuration policies and extension policy entries; boundary cardinality is constant per export invocation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The workflow is intentionally serial: configuration load, product read/fetch, merge/serialization, output write, then native exit. No scheduling changed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: This one-shot export process has no warm cache; the environment path selects local-file versus GitHub retrieval exactly as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete command path and all direct boundary operations were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Network duration and policy count vary, but the diff has zero effect on them.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; boundary count, serialization scale, and critical-path ordering are unchanged.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: When attachments and a GitHub token are present, repository ID resolution precedes upload; the changed Authorization header assignment occurs before the same fetch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch GitHub repository metadata to resolve its numeric ID.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one lookup for the applicable submission due to the caller's local repoId coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same fetch used the same Authorization header key via bracket notation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before uploads; header construction is equivalent and adds no request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sequential native-host call per uncached upload file, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Uploads are awaited serially, but this method and its scheduling are outside the changed hunk.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One repository lookup per submission path that needs it, coalesced by the local repoId value, and existing sequential uploads scale with attachment count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Repository lookup is memoized within the submission through repoId ??=. File uploads remain sequential in the existing for-of loop; the diff changes neither.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The repository ID is reused within one submission but not retained globally. Existing attachment-cache behavior is unaffected.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: caller coalescing, fetch placement, and upload loop were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Attachment size/count and network latency vary, but no changed mechanism affects them.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable network, IPC, or concurrency regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Webview resource loading through the service worker
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each matching GET/HEAD fetch checks the resource cache, sends the existing load-resource message to parent clients, awaits the host response, then builds the response. The modified line only spells the same ETag response-header assignment differently.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Post a load-resource message to each resolved outer iframe client and await the host response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request-store entry per resource fetch and one postMessage per existing parent client; cache state can yield a 304 body reuse but does not eliminate the host validation message.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical cache lookup, parent-client fan-out, host wait, and ETag value under bracket notation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The response awaits the host message; the changed ETag header assignment occurs only while constructing the response and adds no IPC.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Host-side resource loading requested by the service-worker IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one host load request per service-worker resource fetch after parent-client routing, unchanged by the modified header key syntax.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same host resource request and conditional-cache flow existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Potentially on the webview resource critical path, but the diff neither introduces nor reschedules it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of webview resource requests and resolved parent clients; one host request identifier per fetch, with fan-out to the same parent-client set as before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing resource requests can overlap; host response bodies retain the existing semaphore limit where enabled. No coalescing, limiter, or concurrency behavior changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: GET requests without ranges continue to open/match the same CacheStorage entry; cached ETags continue to be sent as ifNoneMatch and 304 responses reuse the cached body. The cache key and ETag value are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: fetch dispatch, cache lookup, parent-client fan-out, semaphore, and response construction were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Resource count and backing-provider latency vary by webview, but the PR does not change either.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable cache, IPC, or fan-out regression.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening a replace preview decodes the original scheme from the synthetic URI, resolves the source model, and creates the preview model. The changed JSON property access precedes the same model resolution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the source text model when it is not already available through the model resolver.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One model-reference request per preview model creation, subject to existing resolver reuse.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same parsed scheme and source resource were produced using ['scheme'].
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the preview can render; the changed .scheme lookup does not change the resource identity or resolution count.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One JSON parse and source-model resolution per opened replace preview; existing search-result filtering scales with current matches.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing async model-reference resolution remains unchanged; no new parallelism or serialization is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Text-model reference reuse remains owned by the existing resolver service; the synthetic URI and query payload are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the URI conversion and immediate caller were inspected and are semantically identical.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Whether model resolution incurs I/O depends on model warmth, but the diff does not affect warm/cold selection.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable serialization, I/O, or repeated-work regression.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 23 changed files and all diff pages. The PR consistently replaces static-key bracket notation with equivalent dot notation (plus allowlist/test updates); no changed hunk adds expensive work, increases multiplicity, changes cache lifecycle, alters concurrency, or moves an existing boundary onto a hotter path. No performance findings were submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
